hardWonLessons.axum08PathParams: axum 0.8.9 (Cargo.toml line 221). Two route entries whose paths differ only by parameter name (e.g. /events/{type} and /events/{id}) conflict, and registering the same path twice with separate .route() calls panics with an overlapping-method-route error. When the TypeScript source has one path with two verbs (GET /events/:type and PATCH /events/:id), register ONE route entry with a combined method router: .route("/events/{id}", get(read_event).patch(update_event)). The externally visible path is unchanged.
hardWonLessons.routeInventory: When porting a TypeScript router, enumerate EVERY verb: router.get/post/put/patch/delete, not just a get/post/put/delete subset. A 'patch' route was missed in the first slice-2 brief.
hardWonLessons.malformedBody: Axum's Json extractor rejects a malformed body BEFORE the handler runs, returning plain text instead of the source's JSON envelope. Express body-parser throws inside the try block, so the source answers {error:true,message:'Internal server error',status:500}. Use Option<Json<Value>> and map the absent case to that envelope to preserve parity.
hardWonLessons.mongooseUpdateSemantics: Mongoose findByIdAndUpdate(id, plainObject) performs a partial update (it wraps the object in $set), returns the post-update document with {new:true}, strips _id and __v from the payload, runs schema validators ONLY with runValidators:true (the source omits it), and does NOT fire pre('save') hooks - so updatedAt is not refreshed on that path.
hardWonLessons.mongooseUpsertSemantics: Mongoose updateOne(filter, {$setOnInsert: body}, {upsert:true}) applies setDefaultsOnInsert (a schema default for any path absent from $setOnInsert is written on insert), casts BOTH the $setOnInsert payload AND the filter's equality fields, builds the upserted document as the filter's equality fields MERGED with the $setOnInsert payload, stores a JavaScript number as a BSON Double, and STRIPS undefined update paths (an undefined value is absent from the stored document, not null). Mongoose's updateOne does NOT run validators by default - only save() does. Native remedy that already exists in this repo: SchemaDefinition::construct(&merged_doc, now) applies defaults and casts (it also runs the required/enum validators, which Mongoose's update path does not, so it is strictly narrower); hydrate() does the same without validators but is gated behind the command-reward-schemas feature. Do NOT write a parallel ad-hoc caster - use the schema framework or report a framework gap.
hardWonLessons.mongoNumericType: The native framework's js_number helper (dimabot/src/utils/bson_compat.rs:15) reproduces the Node BSON rule: an integral finite number inside the Int32 range becomes Bson::Int32, everything else becomes Bson::Double. A JavaScript number is NOT always stored as a BSON Double - an earlier lead claim to that effect was wrong and is withdrawn. Do not write assertions that contradict the framework.
hardWonLessons.routeOracleRequiresMatchingSeam: A route-layer oracle requires the native route to expose the SAME seam set the source oracle stubs. A native that hard-wires its data access can never be compared against a stubbed source. This composes with the data-layer slice: the data layer is verified against a disposable Mongo plus its own source oracle, the route layer against the source stubbed data - neither needs the other Mongo.
hardWonLessons.oracleStubMustReproduceMiddlewareRejecti: An oracle stub for a middleware must reproduce that middleware's REJECTION behaviour, not only its happy path. A pass-through stub silently changes the source's observable behaviour and forces the comparison onto an unrealistic path: it made the source produce a route-level fallback envelope the real source can never produce, and forced the native onto an unprotected builder it never uses in production.

oracleFixtureMechanism.purpose: The repository's actual-source oracle pattern. Any slice that needs source-vs-native comparison should follow it instead of inventing a new harness.
oracleFixtureMechanism.oracleSide: dimabot/tests/fixtures/<name>_reference.cjs - pins the source SHA-256, transpiles the REAL .ts with ts.transpileModule, runs it in a real Express app with the production body-parser order, mocks only the necessary seams, and exposes --write <abs-dir> / --check <abs-dir> modes writing <name>-reference.json.
oracleFixtureMechanism.routeTemplate: dimabot/tests/fixtures/observability_route_reference.cjs (route oracle); dimabot/tests/fixtures/api_auth_reference.cjs (fixture JSON shape and consumption contract); dimabot/tests/fixtures/mongoose_set_on_insert_reference.cjs (disconnected mongoose mocking, setDefaultsOnInsert, pinned node 24.22.1 / mongoose 8.24.2 / bson 6.10.4).
oracleFixtureMechanism.nativeSide: A support module exposing fixture() (reads DIMA_<NAME>_FIXTURE_DIR, which must be absolute and outside the workspace, plus DIMA_<NAME>_FIXTURE_SHA256 lowercase hex, verifies the digest, loads <dir>/<name>-reference.json), fixture_case(), fixture_case_names() and assert_case(fixture, name, status, body). See dimabot/tests/support/api_auth_support.rs.
oracleFixtureMechanism.testShape: #[ignore = "requires the external source oracle fixture"] tests that pin the case-name list and assert each case's status and body through assert_case.
oracleFixtureMechanism.important: The .cjs is AUTHORED by the team but RUN by the integration team in a later leased phase with the pinned isolated Node/TypeScript toolchain. Never run node in the authoring wave.
oracleFixtureMechanism.knownLimitation: dimabot/tests/support/api_auth_support.rs Provider routes only /oauth2/validate and /helix/users, so it CANNOT serve a Helix streams board. A route/collector slice needing one must add its own task-owned loopback recorder in its own new support file; api_auth_support.rs is shared and must not be modified.
